traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Magnoliaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate or palmate; leaves evergreen or deciduous; stipules present; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely monoecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually tepals, sometimes spiral, rarely sepals and petals; fruit follicle or aggregate, rarely samara; stamens (8-) 50 to 200; carpels (2-) 20 to 200. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.bract_form.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 72, family Magnoliaceae: bract form spathe; one or more circular bracts enclose the flower and are shed at anthesis; read as "spathe".

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Magnoliales page (read 2026-10-16): Magnoliaceae leaves spiral, growth sympodial; differs from the two-ranked order.

traits.flowering_position.note: APweb, Magnoliales page (read 2026-10-16): Magnoliaceae flowers terminal; axillary-looking flowers in the Michelia group (our addition, medium confidence).

traits.perianth_parts.note: FNA vol. 3, Magnoliaceae (F. G. Meyer), family account via eFloras taxon 10530 (read 2026-10-18): "tepals deciduous, 6-18, in 3 or more whorls of 3"; the genus Magnolia "tepals 9-15". Read as 9 to 15, 6 to 18 at the extremes.

traits.stamen_form.note: FNA vol. 3, Magnoliaceae (F. G. Meyer), family account via eFloras taxon 10530 (read 2026-10-18): "stamens numerous ... filaments very short to 1/2 length of anthers; ... connective with distal appendage"; Flora of China, Magnolia grandiflora: "filaments purple, flat; connective exserted and forming a mucro". A flat stamen whose anther takes most of its length: read as laminar.

traits.floral_receptacle.note: FNA vol. 3, Magnoliaceae (F. G. Meyer), family account via eFloras taxon 10530 (read 2026-10-18): "pistils numerous, superior, spirally arranged on elongate receptacle (torus)"; genus Magnolia: "stamens on elongate torus".
